t: Section 704(c) of the Veterans Benefits Act of 2003 (38 U.S.C. 5101 note) is amended by striking “December 31, 2012” and inserting “December 31, 2013”.

fable.w: This section only extends an expiration date in an existing statute by one year. The tempting reading is that the underlying veterans benefits authority might involve outside parties, but nothing in this text calls for consultation, comment, hearings, advisory bodies, or a right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. A bare date amendment creates no participation process.
fable.s: is amended by striking “December 31, 2012” and inserting “December 31, 2013”

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple technical amendment that extends a deadline by one year. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, public comment, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. It is purely an internal legislative adjustment to a date.
qwen_block.s: Section 704(c) of the Veterans Benefits Act of 2003 (38 U.S.C. 5101 note) is amended by striking “December 31, 2012” and inserting “December 31, 2013”.

opus.w: This amendment only changes a date, replacing "December 31, 2012" with "December 31, 2013" in an existing provision of the Veterans Benefits Act of 2003. It might be tempting to assume the underlying provision involves outside parties, such as contract medical examiners. But the text in front of us sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue that brings anyone outside the federal government into a federal decision.
